chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

In the case of a mukatab (a slave contracted for manumission) who had a free woman under his ownership, she made a will to him upon her death. The heirs said: 'We do not validate his will, for he is a mukatab who has not yet been freed and does not inherit.' He ruled: 'He inherits according to the portion of him that has been freed, and the will is valid for him according to the portion of him that has been freed.'
And he ruled in the case of a mukatab who was bequeathed a will, and he had paid half of what was due to him, that half of the will was validated.
And he ruled in the case of a mukatab who had paid a quarter of what was due to him, and a will was made to him, that a quarter of the will was validated.
And he said regarding a man who bequeathed to a female mukatab, and she had paid one-sixth of what was due to her, that it was validated for her according to the portion of her that had been freed.

key_terms.أَهْلُ اَلْمِيرَاث: The heirs: Those entitled to inherit the estate.
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: Mukatab: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom.
key_terms.وَصِيَّة: Will/Bequest: A legal disposition of property after death.

ai.seo_question: How is a mukatab's inheritance or bequest calculated based on his manumission progress?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic status of a *mukatab* (slave with a manumission contract) as a partial heir, resolving the dispute among heirs who argued that only fully freed slaves could inherit. It establishes a proportional mechanism where the bequest and inheritance rights scale with the portion of the contract price already paid, reflecting the gradual transition from slavery to freedom. This principle underscores the Shia legal view of *mukatab* as possessing independent financial agency and inheritance rights commensurate with their emancipation progress.
